title: Clearly define senior advisers' portfolios
proposal: The chapter says senior advisers should get the staff they need, and the Chief of Staff should clearly define and announce each adviser's area of responsibility across the White House.
quote: To ensure that senior advisers are effective, their portfolios must be clearly delineated and clearly communicated across the White House.
agency: White House Office / Chief of Staff

title: Reexamine limits on White House–Justice Department contacts
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing the long-standing rule that White House contact with the Justice Department go only through the White House Counsel and top DOJ leaders, and considering more channels of communication.
quote: The next Administration should reexamine this policy and determine whether it might be more efficient or more appropriate for communication to occur through additional channels.

title: Review major lawsuits and consider reversing prior positions
proposal: The White House Counsel should quickly review major ongoing lawsuits across the executive branch and recommend to the President whether to reconsider or reverse the previous administration's legal positions.
quote: including recommendations for reconsidering or reversing positions of the previous Administration in any significant litigation.

title: Pick a White House Counsel chosen for loyalty and broad experience
proposal: The President should choose a White House Counsel with wide legal experience who is, above all, loyal to the President and the Constitution, rather than a specialist chosen for elite credentials.
quote: while a candidate with elite credentials might seem ideal, the best one will be above all loyal to the President and the Constitution.

title: Reconsider permanent press space at the White House
proposal: The chapter notes there is no legal right to permanent media space on the White House grounds and recommends reexamining how much space is given to the press.
quote: the next Administration should reexamine the balance between media demands and space constraints on the White House premises.

title: Consider replacing the White House Correspondents' Association role
proposal: The administration should review its relationship with the White House Correspondents' Association and consider whether a different group should coordinate press matters.
quote: The new Administration should examine the nature of the relationship between itself and the White House Correspondents Association and consider whether an alternative coordinating body might be more suitable.

title: Plan early for political workforce needs, such as Schedule F
proposal: The Office of Presidential Personnel should identify the administration's political workforce needs early and develop plans for them, with Schedule F given as an example.
quote: Identifying programmatic political workforce needs early and developing plans (for example, Schedule F).

title: Make the personnel office directly responsible for hirings and firings
proposal: The Office of Presidential Personnel should play the 'bad cop' role, including taking direct responsibility for hiring and firing political staff.
quote: Playing “bad cop” in a way that other White House offices cannot (including serving as the office that takes direct responsibility for firings and hirings).

title: Use the personnel office as a link to conservative organizations
proposal: The Office of Presidential Personnel should serve as a link between conservative organizations and the executive branch for filling jobs.
quote: Serving as a personnel link between conservative organizations and the executive branch.

title: Keep political staff in place just below senior agency leaders
proposal: The chapter says departments and agencies should have strong groups of political appointees just below senior levels so they are ready if top jobs suddenly become vacant.
quote: it is necessary to ensure that departments and agencies have robust cadres of political staff just below senior levels in the event of unexpected vacancies.

title: Hold regular meetings of Deputy Secretaries
proposal: The Office of Cabinet Affairs should organize regular meetings of department Deputy Secretaries, who often become acting secretaries when Cabinet members leave.
quote: It should also organize and administer regular meetings of the Deputy Secretaries because they also typically serve vital roles in the departments and agencies

title: Expand Cabinet Affairs' tracking of the President's agenda
proposal: The Office of Cabinet Affairs should expand its role in tracking the President's agenda and working with each department to advance policy priorities.
quote: It has worked with each department and agency to advance policy priorities. In the future, amplifying this function would truly benefit both the President and the

title: Choose a Public Liaison director without lobbying ties
proposal: The head of the Office of Public Liaison should come from the President's campaign or Capitol Hill and should not have deep ties to a lobbying firm or other interested party.
quote: but should not have deeply entrenched connections to a K Street entity or any other potential stakeholder.

title: Assign overlapping policy areas to a single council
proposal: Where the National Security, Economic, and Domestic Policy Councils overlap, such as immigration or trade, the White House should assign each topic to only one council when possible.
quote: Identifying these potentially problematic areas and assigning policy responsibilities to only one council where possible will help to speed up the policy-coordination process.
agency: White House policy councils (NSC, NEC, DPC)

title: Have policy councils lead on China, immigration, energy and 'wokeism'
proposal: The White House policy councils should quickly lead work on cross-agency priorities: countering China, enforcing immigration laws, reversing rules to boost energy production, defending life and religious liberty, and confronting 'wokeism' in government.
quote: incoming policy councils will need to move rapidly to lead policy processes around cross-cutting agency topics, including countering China, enforcing
agency: White House policy councils (NSC, NEC, DPC)

title: Limit detailees on the National Security Council staff
proposal: The administration should limit the number of staff loaned to the National Security Council from other agencies so the President has more direct control.
quote: The next Administration should try to limit the number of detailees to ensure more direct presidential control.

title: Domestic Policy Council head should chair regular EOP meetings
proposal: The Domestic Policy Council director should lead a standing meeting with the heads of other Executive Office of the President offices to improve coordination.

title: Create an economic opportunity working group
proposal: The President should create a working group, led by the Domestic Policy Council director, to coordinate policies that promote economic opportunity.
quote: The President should establish an economic opportunity working group, chaired by the DPC Director, to

title: Coordinate domestic and security councils on border security
proposal: The Domestic Policy Council should work with the National Security Council on a plan to strengthen border security.
quote: Finally, DPC should coordinate with the NSC on a policy agenda to enhance border security.
